correctness.rationale: The exact 63-state finite Markov first-step system is uniquely solvable. The complement argument exhaustively identifies K3,3 and triangular prism as the only connected cubic graphs on six vertices. Their 9- and 12-orbit exact symbolic solutions produce six rational gap identities for uniform initial k-subsets, k=1,...,6. Each reduces to c^3 times one of four explicitly stated polynomials with all coefficients positive divided by positive factors. This is an infinite-parameter proof, not a grid inference. Six unreduced rational 63-state solves independently validate 36 exact graph-by-rate-by-k means at c=1/3,1,3. At c=0, all k-subsets have mean H_k. The result does not cover arbitrary fixed initial patterns or different dynamics.

value.rationale: A natural minimal complete comparison of the two connected cubic six-patch graphs holds uniformly for all six possible initial occupation counts, despite identical degree, edge, distance and Perron data; it also implies strict advantage for any identically independently occupied initial habitat distribution with positive occupation probability. This exact global and initial-state-robust dominance provides a meaningful finite-population ecological topology benchmark and boundary to spectral proxy rankings, not a small arbitrary numerical gain.
